findings.text: Demultiplexing entry resolves a hardware number inside a supplied domain to a descriptor, attempts cross processor redirection, otherwise dispatches through generic descriptor handling and reports the handling outcome, with a missing mapping reported as unhandled.

Remote redirection is declined when the current processor is already covered by effective affinity, offered first to an optional pre redirect hook, and only active descriptors queue work to a stored target processor; an alternate build always declines.

Handler presence is checked under the descriptor lock to exclude shutdown races, and queued work is ordered against processor teardown so it either lands before offline marking and is later flushed or observes an already migrated target.
Lookup helper returns the numeric identifier of the first descriptor at or after a supplied offset, falling back to the total count when none exists, under read side protection.
Descriptor release helper drops the descriptor raw lock with saved flags and conditionally performs bus synchronization unlock.

Statistics helpers expose per processor counts, summed totals, local increment, snapshot of current counters into reference values, delta since snapshot, and a read locked user total, all yielding zero for unknown numbers.
Summation uses a single total for ordinary lines and aggregates per processor counters across the supplied mask for per processor or non maskable lines.
Classification helper assigns distinct lockdep classes to descriptor lock and request mutex when the descriptor exists.
Firmware identifier wrapper holds an embedded firmware handle, a parent handle, a type tag, an allocated name string, and a physical address pointer.
Firmware operations expose name and parent by recovering the wrapper from its embedded handle.
Firmware node allocator builds a wrapper with a formatted name varying by type and initializes the handle with chip operations, failing cleanly on allocation failure.
Simple and legacy domain constructors populate size, hardware range, virtual base and host data and instantiate a domain, returning null on error.
Simple domains cover zero to size while legacy domains shift the window by a hardware base and request direct mapping support.
Matching scan holds the global domain mutex while walking the domain list and applying select, match, or firmware plus bus token equality, with a wildcard token bypassing select.
Default domain accessor returns the current global default pointer, possibly null.

Disassociation validates ownership, marks the line unavailable for request, detaches chip and handler, waits for in flight handling, notifies the unmap hook, issues a barrier, clears association, decrements use count and removes reverse mapping, all under the root mutex.

Direct mapping allocator defaults the domain, allocates a descriptor above zero, enforces a hardware maximum, associates an identity hardware to virtual number, and frees the descriptor on any failure.

Affinity aware creation reuses an existing hardware to virtual association when present and otherwise allocates and associates under the root mutex, defaulting a null domain to the global default and rejecting a null default.
Firmware spec translation prefers a hierarchy translate hook, then a legacy translate hook, otherwise copies the first cell as the hardware number.
Helper converts a device node plus raw cells into a firmware spec by capturing the handle, count and values.
Domain resolution for a spec prefers a wired bus match, falls back to a wildcard match, and uses the default domain when the spec carries no firmware reference.
Spec info query zeroes the caller record and delegates to the domain hook when available, otherwise reports absence without failure.

Firmware spec mapping proceeds through domain lookup, translation and sense filtering, existing mapping reuse with trigger compatibility handling, then hierarchical versus flat allocation, and finally trigger storage; mismatched configured triggers or missing data abort with zero while the lock is held except for a wired MSI allocation window.
Wired MSI allocator validates device and bus token, packs type and hardware number into a cookie, and allocates at any index under the device MSI guard, returning a virtual number or negative error.
Device domain lookup requires the caller to hold the device MSI mutex, bounds checks the domain identifier, and rejects absent or parent domains.

Indexed allocation helper obtains the domain, allocates a descriptor with optional affinity copy and cookie, inserts at a requested or automatic position respecting hardware size, runs domain allocation over a single index range, and unwinds on failure, reporting index and virtual number.
Storage insertion honors hardware capacity, with automatic choice picking a free slot within limits and explicit choice validating range, and any failure releases the descriptor.
Hardware size comes from domain info when a domain is present, otherwise it falls back to a default store size.

Bulk MSI allocation prepares a per domain argument, derives activation and reservation flags, iterates stored descriptors in range skipping already associated ones, invokes prepare and set hooks, allocates virtual numbers, links descriptors, initializes each vector, optionally publishes filesystem entries, and aborts on first error.
Descriptor filter distinguishes all entries from unassociated versus associated based on presence of a virtual number.
Filesystem publisher creates per vector read only attributes named by virtual number and wired to mode display, cleaning up all published entries on any failure.
A global domain mutex serializes list matching while each hierarchy root mutex serializes mapping creation, association and teardown.
